idiom_name: assert! / debug_assert! macros plus type-level invariants
implementation_notes: Rust ships assert! and assert_eq! in core: they always run and panic, while debug_assert! and debug_assert_eq! run in non-optimized builds by default and disappear under optimization unless -C debug-assertions is passed. The split mirrors C's NDEBUG with an explicit knob. Idiomatic Rust pushes invariants further with private fields, newtypes and exhaustive enums; use Result for caller-supplied failures, assert! for a runtime invariant that must survive release, and debug_assert! only for supplemental checks too expensive for production. Panic unwinds with a message (or aborts under panic = abort), and stdlib APIs document their invariants in a # Panics section.
pitfalls: debug_assert! is compiled out in optimized builds with no trace at all, so a violated invariant becomes silent corruption instead of a panic; cargo test --release stops checking it too.
Panicking across an FFI boundary or while unwinding is undefined behaviour in the wrong edition; assert! in cleanup paths needs care.
A panic while a lock guard is held poisons the lock, so invariant checks inside concurrent code must not panic in ways callers cannot anticipate.
The compiler will not tell you which invariants are unchecked: prefer newtypes and private fields over adding more assert! calls.
